newsitem.title: USA: Guidant says halts Ventak AV shipments.
newsitem.headline: Guidant says halts Ventak AV shipments.

text.p: Guidant Corp said it stopped international shipments and implants of its Ventak AV AICD automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator based on observations of some implanted devices in Europe.

The product, not approved for U.S. marketing, is Guidant's newest implantable defibrillator. Such devices are implanted in the chest or abdomen of a patient and connected by wires to the heart to keep it from beating too fast.
The CPI unit of Guidant said it "has identified a small number of implanted Ventak AV devices that have experienced an abnormal rise in pacing impedance and pacing threshold."
The problem "has resulted in loss of pacing capture in a few cases," the company said.
Guidant continued, "This observation does not affect the device's ability to deliver defibrillation therapy if needed by the patient."
Shares in Guidant were off 1 to 54-3/4.
Guidant said it is taking steps to resolve the situation and expects to resume implants within four to six weeks.
"Guidant is in the process of communicating this situation and the proposed corrective action to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration," it said.
"At this time, Guidant does not anticipate any design changes and does not expect this matter to significantly affect the U.S. market release of the Ventak AV," it said.
Guidant said no other product made or distributed by its cardiac rhythm management group is affected.
